message.content:
This is the fix! `fda03e29` fixes an index-out-of-bounds in `h3NeighborRotations` when `oldDigit == INVALID_DIGIT` (7). 

In the vulnerable version, `NEW_DIGIT_II[oldDigit][dir]` and `NEW_ADJUSTMENT_II[oldDigit][dir]` are indexed by `oldDigit`. If `oldDigit == INVALID_DIGIT` (7), then `NEW_DIGIT_II[7][dir]` is out of bounds (the array is `[7][7]`, so valid indices are 0-6).

This is the index-out-of-bounds! The fix adds a check: `if (oldDigit == INVALID_DIGIT) return H3_NULL;`.

So the vulnerability is: when `h3` (from `stringToH3`) has an index digit set to `INVALID_DIGIT` (7), then `h3NeighborRotations` accesses `NEW_DIGIT_II[7][dir]` which is out of bounds.

Now I need to construct an H3 index where some index digit is 7 (INVALID_DIGIT). The fuzzer calls `h3NeighborRotations(h3, DIGITS[i], &rotations)` in a loop. The `h3` comes from `stringToH3(new_str)`.

Let me construct an H3 index with an index digit = 7. The H3 index format:
- Bits 0-3: reserved (4 bits)
- Bits 4-7: mode (4 bits) - should be 1 for cell mode
- Bits 8-11: reserved (4 bits)
- Bits 12-15: base cell (4 bits)
- Bits 16-19: resolution (4 bits)
- Bits 20-63: index digits (7 bits each, 15 digits for resolutions 1-15)

Wait, let me check the H3 index layout. Let me look at the h3Index.h header.
